concept.title: Pseudo-elements
concept.shortdesc: A pseudo-element starts with :: and targets a special part or state associated with an element. It appears after the element selector:

section.title: Text parts
section.p: ::first-line selects the first formatted line of text. ::first-letter selects the first typographic letter or punctuation group.
Use these selectors to style the first formatted line or typographic letter of an element.

section.title: Generated content, markers and footnotes
section.p: CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §4, Tree-Abiding Pseudo-elements; CSS GCPM 3 §1.1.1, The string-set property; CSS GCPM 3 §1.1.1.1, The content() function; CSS GCPM 3 §1.1.2, The string() function; CSS GCPM 3 §2.6, The footnote-call pseudo-element; CSS GCPM 3 §2.7, The footnote-marker pseudo-element.

::before and ::after identify generated-content positions before or after an element’s content. The content property supplies their content. ::marker targets a list marker. The footnote pseudo-elements identify a footnote call and marker.
Paged CSS also defines string-set to copy an element’s text into a named string for reuse, for example in a page margin box. See Named strings for how to use string-set and string().

The content property specifies what ::before and ::after contain. A selector alone does not add text. The list marker’s content can come from content or the list-marker properties. Footnote pseudo-elements mark the call and marker parts of a footnote.

section.title: Highlight pseudo-elements
section.p: ::selection identifies text selected by the user. ::search-text identifies text found by a search. ::target-text identifies text targeted by a document link. ::spelling-error and ::grammar-error identify ranges marked by spelling and grammar checking. ::highlight(name) selects a named text range registered through the Custom Highlight API.
These ranges are defined by selection, search, navigation, spelling and grammar checking, or script-provided highlights. They are not ordinary XML elements.

section.title: Element-backed pseudo-elements
section.p: CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §4, Tree-Abiding Pseudo-elements; CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §5, Element-backed Pseudo-Elements; CSS Position 4 §3.2, The ::backdrop Pseudo-Element.

::placeholder targets placeholder text in a control. ::file-selector-button targets a file-upload control’s button. ::details-content targets the expandable content of a disclosure control. ::backdrop targets the backdrop behind an element presented in the top layer.
These pseudo-elements refer to parts of controls or elements defined by the document language. Their meaning depends on the host language’s control and presentation behavior.

CSSMedia also accepts ::before::marker, ::after::marker, ::first-letter::prefix and ::first-letter::suffix. These select marker content associated with generated ::before or ::after content, and punctuation around a ::first-letter part. A supported state pseudo-class can follow a pseudo-element, but interaction states such as :hover do not match.
